vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes skip the cool-down (Renovate's default for vulnerability alerts), are never merged without a person, and carry release:now, so merging one releases at once (release.yml) instead of waiting for the weekly release.

hostRules.description: dhi.io (Docker Hardened Images, the runtime base) serves only a logged-in Docker account. The two secrets are Renovate's own, set in the Mend developer portal for this repository (not the GitHub Actions secrets of the same names).

lockFileMaintenance.description: Done by lock-maintenance.yml instead, with a cool-down: Renovate's own refreshes every transitive dependency to whatever was published a minute ago (minimumReleaseAge does not apply to it).

customManagers.description: Tool versions in Dockerfile ARGs, marked with a `# renovate: datasource=... depName=...` comment on the line above (cargo-chef, cargo-about). FanFicFare is in python/pyproject.toml + uv.lock (pep621 manager; lock file maintenance refreshes everything under it).
The BuildKit image CI builds with (image.yml, setup-buildx driver-opts), pinned by digest because its layer compression is part of the reproducible image digest.

Tool versions in workflows, marked with a `# renovate: datasource=... depName=...` comment on the line above a `version:`-style input: uv (setup-uv, ci.yml), Syft (sbom-action) and Grype (scan-action). Syft and Grype are pinned because the actions' bundled defaults lag: Syft 1.54 listed every package of the DHI base twice (it reads both /var/lib/dpkg/status and status.d), which doubled every finding in the Security tab.

The web UI's self-hosted scripts (npm packages) in the vendor lock. Renovate edits only the `version` line; the vendor-sync workflow then downloads the files and fills in the hashes on the same branch (the hosted app cannot run post-upgrade commands).
Tools in the vendor lock, released on GitHub with a `v` tag (the Tailwind CSS compiler). vendor-sync fills in each platform's sha256 from the release's sha256sums.txt.

packageRules.description: Base images: the Rust image and the Python image move independently of Cargo/pip, so keep them out of the dependency PRs.
GitHub Actions are pinned by commit; take them together.
uv is pinned twice, the image's (Dockerfile, uv stage) and CI's (setup-uv in ci.yml): one PR moves both, so CI's venv is built by the uv the image is.
Syft and Grype, the SBOM and the scan: one PR for both, as they read the image the same way.

A new runner OS can break the build in ways CI only half covers: propose it on the dependency dashboard and wait for approval. (The runtime base, dhi.io/python X.Y.Z-debian13, gets version and digest updates like any image; a new Debian release is a new tag suffix, changed by hand, as is a new Python minor version, which ci.yml, the justfile and pyrefly.toml must follow.)
htmx 4 is published under npm's `next` tag (`latest` stays on 2.x until about 2027), so look past `latest` for htmx's updates.

A new major version of a vendored script or of Tailwind changes how the UI's markup behaves (htmx 2 to 4 renamed every event): never automerged, and proposed only once approved on the dependency dashboard.

Automerge patch updates of stable (>= 1.0) dependencies once they are 3 days old (minimumReleaseAge: most malicious releases are found and yanked by then) and the required `ci-ok` check passes (GitHub auto-merge, enforced by the main ruleset). Minor and major updates, and patches of anything still on 0.x (where a patch may break), run CI and wait for a human. Merged updates go out with the weekly release (release.yml). The exceptions come after it, so that they override it.

Digest and pin updates automerge too, at any version: the tag or version stays the same, only the digest it is pinned to changes (a rebuilt base image). Not for GitHub Actions or the build tooling: see the next rules.

GitHub Actions are never automerged, not even a digest update: a tag moved to another commit is exactly how tj-actions/changed-files was compromised (March 2025), and actions run in the jobs that hold the GitHub App's key, the signing identity and the registry token. Commit dates (the release age Renovate sees) can be forged, so the cool-down is no help here.
BuildKit and the Dockerfile frontend build every image, and BuildKit runs privileged on the runner, next to the registry login: reviewed by a person, like the actions.
Container registries do not always give a release time (ghcr.io, dhi.io): without this, minimumReleaseAge would hold those updates back forever. Images that have one still wait.
